newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa - not policy to pressure travel agents.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa - not policy to pressure travel agents.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Monday denied that it had a company policy of putting pressure on travel agents to protect its market share, as was suggested in a German newspaper.
A spokeswoman for the airline told Reuters that there had been an isolated case of such pressure in Northern Bavaria, but said the incident occured without management approval.
"There is no such strategy," she said.

Around 20 travel agents in North Bavaria received a letter from Lufthansa, encouraging them to keep British Airway's share of the German market below 15 percent from mid-October through mid-December this year, or risk getting worse business conditions from Lufthansa.
Germany's Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported the incident in its Monday edition.

"This action by the North Bavarian sales division had not been agreed in any manner with management. We will withdraw the letter in question today. We do not stand over it," Lufthansa's spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman added that cartel authorities had been informed of the incident.
"There will be consequences for the North Bavarian sales division," she said.
